## WaveFlow 1.5.1 — Bug-fix patch

First patch on top of 1.5.0. Mostly quality-of-life fixes around the lyrics waterfall, the library analyzer, and a couple of UI regressions that landed with the skin system.

Thanks to **@jo-el414** for reporting [#279](https://github.com/InstaZDLL/WaveFlow/issues/279), [#280](https://github.com/InstaZDLL/WaveFlow/issues/280), [#281](https://github.com/InstaZDLL/WaveFlow/issues/281), [#284](https://github.com/InstaZDLL/WaveFlow/issues/284), and [#286](https://github.com/InstaZDLL/WaveFlow/issues/286).

---

### 🎤 Lyrics — saner waterfall + manual override

The auto-waterfall (LRCLIB → NetEase → Megalobiz → Genius) used to surface a couple of failure modes:

- Genius pages sometimes shipped only the page header `"N ContributorsTitle Lyrics"` instead of actual lyrics, and the parser dumped that artifact verbatim.
- The source badge always said **LRCLIB** regardless of which provider actually responded, so a Genius-cached bad result looked like a LRCLIB bug.
- No way to recover: "Clear + Refetch" just re-ran the same waterfall and landed on the same hit.

**1.5.1 fixes all three:**

- The Genius parser now strips the `N Contributor(s)<title> Lyrics` header and treats stub catalogue pages (header only, no transcribed body) as a miss so the next provider gets a turn.
- The lyrics source badge shows the **actual provider** that answered (LRCLIB, Genius, NetEase, Megalobiz, Musixmatch).
- Click the badge to open a picker: pick any of the five providers and the lyrics re-fetch from that one only. The miss / hit / re-pick cycle lives entirely in the panel.

Plus a few quieter fixes: the picker closes on **Escape**, and switching tracks during a refetch or import no longer overwrites the new track's lyrics with a stale response.

Closes [#284](https://github.com/InstaZDLL/WaveFlow/issues/284).

---

### 🎚️ Library analysis — cancellable + cooperative

The post-scan **Auto-analyse tracks** sweep used to be a tight loop that decoded every audio file end-to-end with zero breathing room. On large libraries (4 000+ tracks) it pegged a CPU core for 30+ minutes and could effectively freeze mid-tier laptops, with no escape short of force-killing WaveFlow.

**1.5.1 makes it well-behaved:**

- A **Stop** button replaces the **Analyze** button while a run is in flight (Settings → Library). Clicking it stops the analyzer at the next track boundary.
- The worker yields and sleeps 25 ms between tracks so the OS scheduler can interleave the UI, audio playback, and background services like Windows Defender's per-file scan.
- A double-start guard prevents the manual "Analyze library" button from racing the post-scan auto-analyze hook.

Wall-clock cost is roughly 2 % on a 4 000-track library in exchange for the freeze risk going away.

Closes [#286](https://github.com/InstaZDLL/WaveFlow/issues/286).

---

### 🔌 Bundled plugins — no more duplicate copies

Pre-1.5.1, the installer's bundled plugins (Web Radio today) were copied from the resource directory into `%AppData%\Roaming\app.waveflow\waveflow\plugins\` on every boot. That left users with two identical `web-radio` folders on disk and a confusing "why is it in two places?" UX.

**1.5.1 loads bundled plugins straight from the installer's resource directory** — no boot-time copy, no duplicate. Pre-1.5.1 leftovers under the writable plugins tree are removed automatically on first launch.

Closes [#280](https://github.com/InstaZDLL/WaveFlow/issues/280).

---

### 🪟 Mini-player + Skin picker UI fixes

- The **mini-player** booted into a white window since 1.5.0 because of a provider-tree regression introduced with the per-profile theme storage. It opens correctly again. ([#279](https://github.com/InstaZDLL/WaveFlow/issues/279))
- The **Pulse skin** preview in Settings → Appearance leaked its neon halo past the card edge. The preview now shows just the typography + radius — the halo only paints on the real chrome once Pulse is selected. ([#281](https://github.com/InstaZDLL/WaveFlow/issues/281))
- The **About** view's hero card was unreadable in Liquid light because the dark gradient was overridden by Liquid's universal glass treatment, leaving dark-only text classes stranded on pale glass. Hero is now theme-aware and reads correctly on every (skin × theme) combination.

---

Two new keys propagated across all 17 locales:

- **Lyrics → Source picker** — provider names + "Switch source" tooltip + the generic "Online source" fallback label.
- **Settings → Analyze library** — "Stop analysis" button label.

Plenty of plumbing for the upcoming `waveflow-server` shipped under the hood too, but none of it changes the app's local-first model in 1.5.0. ### 🎨 Skins — four new visual identities The theme system grew an orthogonal "skin" axis. **5 skins × 14 themes = 70 combinations**, each persisted per profile. Studio stays as the default Apple-Music-inspired baseline; four new identities land alongside it: - **Editorial** — broadsheet magazine layout, Playfair Display serifs, halftone artwork via `mix-blend-luminosity`, ornate `WaveFlow Gazette` masthead. - **Lounge** — warm burgundy glass over a blurred cover backdrop, Apple-Vibrancy `backdrop-filter` recipe. - **Pulse** — OLED neon-club aesthetic, dual magenta/cyan aurora, vinyl-spin cover that mirrors playback state. - **Liquid** — full Apple Vibrancy with the 8-layer inset `box-shadow` glass recipe, theme-aware (works in light + dark).
Picker lives in **Settings → Appearance** alongside the existing theme picker. Onboarding got a "Pick a vibe" step so first-run users land on the right combo. Motion is dispatched per-skin via Framer Motion — Pulse uses a bouncy spring, calmer skins inherit the soft default. Typography is bundled (Playfair Display, Lora, Space Grotesk, Space Mono, DM Sans Variable) — zero Google Fonts request at runtime. ### 🧩 Plugin SDK — sandboxed WASI plugins (RFC-002) The plugin layer landed as a sandboxed runtime with explicit permission gates: - **WIT + wasmtime** — plugins ship as WASM components compiled against a `waveflow-plugin-sdk` interface (host imports for HTTP, storage, audio, UI). - **Permission gates** — every host import is gated by a manifest declaration the user approves on install. No silent network access, no silent filesystem reach. - **Guardrails by default** — 50 MB max `plugin.wasm` size, 5 s HTTP timeouts, response-body cap, no redirect following (SSRF guard), per-plugin mutex on install/enable/uninstall to close TOCTOU races, offline-mode short-circuit on every outbound request. - **Settings panel** — installed plugins list with one-click enable/disable/uninstall, per-plugin permission chips (network / storage / assets), version + size. ### 📻 Web Radio — the first plugin Ships bundled in the app (so you have something to try the SDK against): a Web Radio plugin that streams internet stations through the same `cpal` engine the rest of the app uses. Stations route through the audio decoder thread so EQ / ReplayGain / spectrum visualizer all work over live streams. Switching stations fast doesn't deadlock — in-flight requests are cancelled cleanly.
### 🎤 Lyrics — multi-provider waterfall + new save modes The lyrics fetcher used to be LRCLIB-only. 1.5.0 ships a dedicated `waveflow-syncedlyrics` crate with **five providers** chained as a graceful fallback: 1. **Musixmatch** (enhanced word-level only) — opt-in, gated on `MUSIXMATCH_ENABLED` env. 2. **LRCLIB** — exact metadata match, primary line-level source. 3. **NetEase** — large Asian catalogue, native LRC. 4. **Megalobiz** — community-scraped enrichment. 5. **Genius** — plain-text last resort. The hidden sidebar is marked `inert` so it can't trap Tab focus or steal pointer events. ### 🧱 Under the hood — `waveflow-server` plumbing (not user-facing yet) Under the hood, a lot of groundwork landed for the future `waveflow-server` companion: tenant-scoped Postgres repositories in `waveflow-core`, auth + sync plumbing, public playlist share canonical IDs, and per-track snapshots in playlist sync ops. **None of this is exposed as a user-facing feature in 1.5.0** — the desktop app remains fully local-first today, and the sync stack will surface in a later release once the server companion is ready. ### 🩹 Quality pass - **Locales** — **579 fixes across 16 locales** over four validator passes, followed by a manual review pass across the non-source languages. ## [1.4.0](https://github.com/InstaZDLL/WaveFlow/compare/v1.3.0...v1.4.0) (2026-05-28)

## ✨ What's new in v1.4.0

WaveFlow 1.4.0 is the **foundations & polish** release — under the hood it lays the groundwork for the upcoming `waveflow-server`, on the surface it cleans up the rough edges you've been reporting against 1.3.0. No flashy new view this time, but the app is steadier, more correct, and Flathub-ready.

### 🧱 Architecture — `waveflow-core` workspace extraction (RFC-001 Phase 1.a)

The Rust backend split into a Cargo workspace with two crates:

- **`waveflow-core`** — portable business logic (domain types, repository traits + SQLite implementations, scanner helpers, smart-playlist engine, audio analysis, DSD format conversion, HTTP clients for Deezer / Last.fm / LRCLIB, artwork pipeline). Zero Tauri, zero `cpal` — designed to be reusable from the future `waveflow-server`.
- **`waveflow`** — the Tauri 2 desktop app. Keeps the `#[tauri::command]` handlers, the real-time `cpal` + `rtrb` audio engine, the DLNA / OS media-controls / Discord RPC integrations, the watcher, tray, profile pool wiring.

End-users won't notice anything different — the desktop app behaves identically. What changes is the future shape of the project: 1.5.0 will start hooking `waveflow-server` on top of the same `waveflow-core` crate so the desktop app and a future browser / mobile client can share scanning, repositories, and metadata enrichment without rewriting them.

### 🎛️ Equalizer — popup ↔ Settings stay in sync (#166)

The player-bar EQ popover and the Settings → Playback EQ card now share live state through a new `player:eq` broadcast. Toggling the master switch, changing presets or nudging a band from either surface updates the other instantly — no more "popup says EQ is on, Settings says off". The popup bypass thumb also lands flush-left when OFF and flush-right when ON instead of looking drifted on Windows. As a bonus, picking an unknown preset key now surfaces an actual error instead of silently no-op'ing.

### 🎤 Lyrics editor — footer always reachable (#172)

The Save / Cancel bar at the bottom of the lyrics editor could be pushed off-screen on 1920×1080 displays with Windows scaling at 125% or higher. The modal now sizes itself like the onboarding wizard (`calc(100vh - 2rem)` + flex-1 body), so the action bar stays pinned at any zoom level.

### 📚 Library — "No cover" filter removed (#170)

The albums-tab "No cover" checkbox was ambiguous enough that several users read it as "hide no-cover albums" and concluded their artwork had vanished. The legitimate use case (find missing covers to backfill) is already covered by **Récupérer toutes les pochettes manquantes** and the per-album cover picker, so the filter is gone for good — one less footgun.

### 🎨 Theming — topbar toggle preserves your family

Picking **Lavender Light** and then clicking the sun/moon toggle now switches to **Lavender** (dark) instead of resetting to the global Émeraude default — and vice-versa for every paired preset (Midnight, Sunset, Lavender, Crimson, Ocean). Themes without a counterpart (OLED, Neon) keep falling back to the global default swap so the toggle still does something sensible.

### 📦 Packaging — Flathub manifest (#164)

A Flatpak manifest landed in tree, ready for submission to Flathub. The build uses the no-default-features path (no in-app updater, since Flatpak owns updates), and the script permissions in the bundle are now correctly non-executable per Flathub's review checklist.

- Theme-pair fix and EQ broadcast cover the visible regressions from 1.3.0 that you reported.
- Phase 1.a went through four rounds of CodeRabbit review before merge — dozens of edge cases caught and fixed (Windows path canonicalisation in playlists, DSD bit-depth ranking in browse SQL, transactional cleanup on profile init failure, file hash recomputation propagation, …).
